short: Tax cuts, a pandemic, two impeachments and a contested departure.
full:
Trump won in 2016 with no prior political or military service, losing the popular vote by nearly three million while carrying the electoral college. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 reduced the corporate rate from 35 to 21 per cent; he appointed three Supreme Court justices, withdrew from the Paris climate accord and the Iran nuclear agreement, and imposed tariffs on China and on steel and aluminium imports.

The House impeached him in December 2019 over pressure on Ukraine to investigate a political rival, and the Senate acquitted him in February 2020. Covid-19 killed some 400,000 Americans before he left office, alongside a federal programme that delivered vaccines within a year. He lost the 2020 election, refused to concede, and a crowd he had addressed stormed the Capitol on 6 January 2021 as the electoral votes were counted. The House impeached him a second time.
